concepts.title: Characteristics of Living Organisms
concepts.definition: Living organisms show certain common characteristics such as growth, movement, respiration, response to stimuli, reproduction, excretion, and the need for food.
concepts.key_idea: All living creatures share a set of life processes that distinguish them from non-living things.
question_patterns: what are the characteristics of living organisms
how can you tell a living thing from a non-living thing
list the common features shown by all living creatures
explain why growth is a characteristic of living things
give one everyday example of characteristics of living organisms

solution_steps.explain: Recall the key characteristics: growth, movement, respiration, response to stimuli, reproduction, excretion, and feeding.

solution_steps.action: Check the object against each process
solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the object being studied shows these life processes or not.
If the object shows these characteristics, it is living; if it shows none, it is non-living, confirming the classification is correct.

worked_examples.question: How can you tell that a plant is a living organism?
worked_examples.solution: A plant grows, needs food and water, responds to light, and reproduces, which are all characteristics of living things.
worked_examples.answer: Because it shows growth, respiration, response to stimuli, and reproduction.

worked_examples.question: Is a stone a living thing? Give a reason.
worked_examples.solution: A stone does not grow, does not breathe, does not respond to stimuli, and does not reproduce.
worked_examples.answer: No, because it shows none of the characteristics of living organisms.

exercises.question: List any five characteristics shown by living organisms.
Explain why a car, though it moves, is not a living thing.

concepts.title: Habitat and Adaptation
concepts.definition: A habitat is the natural surroundings in which an organism lives, and adaptation is the special feature or behaviour that helps an organism survive in its habitat.
concepts.key_idea: Organisms develop adaptations that suit the conditions of their particular habitat.
question_patterns: what is a habitat
what is adaptation
how are animals adapted to their habitat
explain why fish have streamlined bodies
give one everyday example of habitat and adaptation

solution_steps.explain: Determine the natural surroundings where the organism lives, such as water, desert, or forest.
Note the special feature or behaviour that helps the organism survive in that habitat.
Explain how the adaptation matches the habitat conditions, confirming it helps the organism live and reproduce there.

worked_examples.question: How is a fish adapted to live in water?
worked_examples.solution: A fish has a streamlined body to move easily through water, gills to breathe dissolved oxygen, and fins to swim.
worked_examples.answer: Its streamlined body, gills, and fins are adaptations for living in water.

worked_examples.question: Why do desert plants have thick, waxy stems?
worked_examples.solution: Thick stems store water and the waxy coating reduces water loss in the dry desert habitat.
worked_examples.answer: To store water and reduce water loss, which are adaptations to the dry desert habitat.

exercises.question: Define habitat and adaptation with one example each.
Explain how a camel is adapted to survive in the desert.

concepts.title: Plants and Their Parts
concepts.definition: Plants are living organisms with parts such as roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits, each of which performs a specific function needed for the plant's survival.
concepts.key_idea: Different parts of a plant work together to carry out life processes like food-making, water transport, and reproduction.
question_patterns: what are the main parts of a plant
what is the function of roots in a plant
how do leaves help a plant
explain the role of the stem in a plant
give one everyday example of plants and their parts

solution_steps.explain: Name the specific part being studied, such as root, stem, leaf, flower, or fruit.
Describe what that part does, for example roots absorb water, leaves make food, and the stem transports substances.
Explain how the part helps the plant survive and grow, confirming it is essential to the plant's life.

worked_examples.question: What is the function of leaves in a plant?
worked_examples.solution: Leaves make food for the plant using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide through photosynthesis.
worked_examples.answer: Leaves prepare food for the plant by photosynthesis.

worked_examples.question: Why are roots important for a plant?
worked_examples.solution: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil and also anchor the plant firmly in the ground.
worked_examples.answer: Roots absorb water and minerals and hold the plant in the soil.

exercises.question: List the main parts of a plant and state one function of each.
Explain how the stem connects the roots and the leaves.

concepts.title: Animals and Their Body Parts
concepts.definition: Animals are living organisms with body parts such as head, eyes, ears, limbs, and tails, each suited to the animal's way of life and habitat.
concepts.key_idea: The body parts of an animal are structured to help it feed, move, breathe, and sense its surroundings.
question_patterns: what are the main body parts of an animal
how do eyes help an animal
explain the function of limbs in animals
why do animals have different body parts
give one everyday example of animals and their body parts

solution_steps.explain: Name the specific animal body part being studied, such as eyes, ears, limbs, or tail.
Describe what the part does, for example eyes help in seeing and limbs help in moving.
Explain how the body part helps the animal survive in its habitat, confirming its role in feeding, moving, or sensing.

worked_examples.question: How do the eyes of a cat help it survive?
worked_examples.solution: A cat's eyes help it see in low light, which is useful for hunting at night.
worked_examples.answer: The eyes help the cat see and hunt, especially in dim light.

worked_examples.question: Why do birds have wings?
worked_examples.solution: Wings are modified limbs that help birds fly through the air, which is their way of moving and escaping danger.
worked_examples.answer: Wings help birds fly, which is their main mode of movement.

exercises.question: Name three body parts of an animal and state one function of each.
Explain how the body parts of a fish are suited to life in water.

concepts.title: Movement in Animals
concepts.definition: Movement in animals is the ability to change position or move body parts, made possible by structures such as limbs, wings, fins, or muscles.
concepts.key_idea: Different animals move in different ways depending on their body structure and habitat.
question_patterns: how do animals move
what helps animals to move from one place to another
explain how a snake moves without legs
compare movement in fish and birds
give one everyday example of movement in animals

solution_steps.explain: Determine which animal is being studied and where it lives.
Note the body parts used for movement, such as legs, wings, fins, or muscles.
Explain how the animal moves, such as walking, flying, swimming, or crawling, confirming the movement matches its body structure.

worked_examples.question: How does a fish move in water?
worked_examples.solution: A fish uses its fins to push water and its streamlined body to move smoothly forward.
worked_examples.answer: A fish swims using its fins and streamlined body.

worked_examples.question: How does a snake move even though it has no legs?
worked_examples.solution: A snake moves by slithering, using its long body muscles and scales to push against the ground.
worked_examples.answer: A snake slithers using its muscles and body shape to move without legs.

exercises.question: Explain how limbs help land animals to move.
Compare the way a bird and a fish move.

concepts.title: Respiration in Living Organisms
concepts.definition: Respiration is the process by which living organisms take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide while breaking down food to release energy.
concepts.key_idea: All living organisms respire to release energy from food, though the breathing organs may differ.
question_patterns: what is respiration
how do living organisms breathe
explain why respiration is important for living things
how do fish breathe underwater
give one everyday example of respiration in living organisms

solution_steps.explain: Determine which living organism is being studied and where it lives.
Note the organ used for breathing, such as lungs in humans, gills in fish, or stomata in leaves.
Describe how oxygen is used to break down food and release energy, confirming respiration is essential for survival.

worked_examples.question: How do fish breathe underwater?
worked_examples.solution: Fish use gills to absorb dissolved oxygen from water and release carbon dioxide.
worked_examples.answer: Fish breathe through gills that take in dissolved oxygen from water.

worked_examples.question: Why do humans breathe faster while running?
worked_examples.solution: Running needs more energy, so the body uses more oxygen to release energy from food, making us breathe faster.
worked_examples.answer: Because more oxygen is needed to release extra energy during exercise.

exercises.question: Define respiration and explain why it is necessary for living things.
Name the breathing organs in humans, fish, and plants.

concepts.title: Response to Stimuli
concepts.definition: Response to stimuli is the ability of living organisms to react to changes in their surroundings, such as light, heat, sound, or touch.
concepts.key_idea: All living organisms sense changes around them and respond in ways that help them survive.
question_patterns: what is response to stimuli
how do living things respond to their surroundings
explain why a plant grows towards light
how does a human respond to a loud sound
give one everyday example of response to stimuli

solution_steps.explain: Determine the change in the surroundings, such as light, heat, sound, or touch, that acts on the organism.
Note how the organism reacts to the stimulus, such as moving towards light or pulling away from heat.
Describe how the response helps the organism survive, confirming that responding to stimuli is a characteristic of living things.

worked_examples.question: Why does a plant bend towards a window where there is sunlight?
worked_examples.solution: The plant responds to the stimulus of light by growing towards it so its leaves can make more food.
worked_examples.answer: The plant responds to light by bending towards it to get more sunlight for food-making.

worked_examples.question: How does a human respond when touching a hot object?
worked_examples.solution: The heat stimulus causes the hand to pull away quickly to avoid injury.
worked_examples.answer: The person quickly pulls the hand away, which is a response to the heat stimulus.

exercises.question: Define stimulus and response with one example each.
Explain how response to stimuli helps an animal survive.

concepts.title: Growth and Reproduction
concepts.definition: Growth is the increase in size and number of cells in an organism, and reproduction is the process by which living organisms produce new individuals of their own kind.
concepts.key_idea: All living organisms grow and eventually reproduce to continue their species.
question_patterns: what is growth in living organisms
what is reproduction
why do living organisms reproduce
explain how a seed grows into a plant
give one everyday example of growth and reproduction

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the question is about growth (increase in size) or reproduction (producing new individuals).
Explain how the organism grows, such as a seedling becoming a tree, or how it reproduces, such as a hen laying eggs.
Explain how growth and reproduction help the organism survive and continue its kind, confirming these are characteristics of living things.

worked_examples.question: How does a seed grow into a plant?
worked_examples.solution: When a seed gets water, air, and warmth, it germinates and grows roots, a stem, and leaves, becoming a young plant.
worked_examples.answer: The seed germinates and gradually grows into a plant with roots, stem, and leaves.

worked_examples.question: How do animals reproduce?
worked_examples.solution: Animals reproduce by laying eggs or by giving birth to young ones, depending on the type of animal.
worked_examples.answer: Animals reproduce either by laying eggs or by giving birth to young ones.

exercises.question: Define growth and reproduction and give one example of each.
Explain why reproduction is important for the survival of a species.

solution_template.explain: A plant grows, needs food and water, responds to light, and reproduces, which are all characteristics of living things.
